title: refactor-ci-optimize-cache-parallelism-split-lint-test-release
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: The monolithic CI workflows were causing long queue times and repeated cache misses across lint/test/release jobs. This PR splits and refactors the workflows to improve parallelism, reduce redundant caching, and make release automation more robust. Summary of changes: - Split large .github/workflows/ci.yml into lint.yml, test.yml, and release.yml with a shared reusable workflow for node/matrix setup. - Introduce a workspace-aware cache key helper (scripts/cache-key.sh) to reduce cross-job cache churn and improve hit rates. - Rework the test matrix to run unit/integration/e2e pipelines in parallel but gated by changed paths to avoid waste. - Deduplicate node setup steps into .github/actions/setup-node (composite action) to centralize node version pinning and restore-cache semantics. - Add lightweight cache warmers triggered by nightly cron to avoid cold-cache penalties for the main release branch. - Update release automation: make the release job dependent on a successful canary job and add stricter semver validation. Backwards compatibility: No changes to runtime code or public SDK APIs. CI-only refactor. Rollout plan: merge to main and monitor CI queue time, cache hit ratio, and release job latency. If regressions observed, revert to previous commit and re-evaluate cache key heuristics. Checklist: - [x] Split workflows and add reusable composites - [x] Add cache-key helper + unit tests for key generation - [x] Update release action and add semver validation - [x] Run full CI on feature branch and iterate on flaky tests - [x] Update CONTRIBUTING.md with workflow changes Testing: ran local act-emulation, full GitHub Actions run on feature branch (see ci_checks), and validated release dry-run. Related: ENG-3241 (CI queue reduction), ENG-3302 (release robustness).

review_comments: Evan Cho: Great direction — splitting the workflows should help parallelism. A couple of asks: (1) can we limit the integration test matrix when core infra files aren't changed? (2) consider using the repo SHA in cache keys alongside path-based fingerprints to avoid accidental collisions.
Priya Natarajan: Thanks Evan — added a changed-paths gate to integration tests and updated the cache-key helper to include an abbreviated repo SHA when the branch is not main.
Mariana Silva: The release job change LGTM but please add semver validation to prevent malformed tags from triggering downstream artifacts.
Priya Natarajan: Added tools/ci/validate-semver.js and wired it into the release workflow; release step now fails fast on invalid tags.
Liam O'Connor: Observability request — can we emit metrics for cache hit/miss from the warmer and include a small dashboard in docs?
Priya Natarajan: Added a note in docs/ci-workflows.md with Prometheus counters emitted by the warmer (cache_hit/cache_miss) and a sample Grafana panel.

release_notes: Refactor CI: split monolithic ci.yml into lint/test/release workflows
Improve cache hit rates with workspace-aware cache-key helper
Add nightly cache warmer to reduce cold-cache latency
Harden release automation with semver validation and canary gating
Centralize node setup in a reusable composite action
notes: Observed improvement in CI queue time (~25%) on main branch after deploying cache warmers in the canary run.
Cache hit ratio increased from ~42% to ~72% for test caches during the first 48 hours post-merge.
Follow-ups: instrument finer-grained cache metrics per-package and run a two-week experiment on different cache key strategies (ENG-3401).
